title: Every custom Avro property the producer declared reaches at least one flattened leaf
rationale: getObjectProps had never been called anywhere in this library before this API, so property preservation is a brand-new published claim with no corpus row. It is squarely fidelity-relevant: the properties ARE what the consumer gets back, and a governance pipeline's physical-type cascade reads them. The set comparison is chosen so that inheritance, which multiplies a record-level property across N leaves, does not register as divergence; placement is recorded separately and pinned byte-exactly without being the verdict.
catchesBugClass: getObjectProps ceasing to be called; the merge order inverting so an inherited property shadows a field's own, which is visible in propertyPlacement; reserved-key structural metadata leaking into user properties, which would grow the set.
cannotCatch: Set equality alone cannot tell WHICH leaf carries a property - that is why placement is recorded, but placement is pinned, not judged. It also cannot see properties whose names collide with the library's private reserved list; the sibling DEFECT fixture exists precisely because this one is blind to that.

predicted.detail: The declared set and the emitted set are the same four key=value pairs.

configDescription: assert ENRICHED_METADATA vs PROPERTY_SET, default FlattenOptions
